content.json:
# 🛰️ Azure Maintenance Ledger
*Planned and unplanned maintenance of your Azure services, kept as a durable history.* **Exposure** (how long an event was open) and **downtime** (minutes a resource was Unavailable) are different measures and are never added together.

Orange = unplanned, blue = planned. Pick a time range and filters, then choose a tab.

parameters.name: Subscriptions
parameters.label: Subscriptions

parameters.name: Category
parameters.label: Category

parameters.name: Service
parameters.label: Service
parameters.query:
let rows = union
    (AzMaintenance_EventServices({IncludeSynthetic}) | summarize by service),
    (AzMaintenance_Catalog({IncludeSynthetic}) | summarize by service = service_name)
    | summarize by service
    | project value = service, label = service;
let n = toscalar(rows | count);
rows
| union (print value = "(no data yet)", label = "(no data yet)" | where n == 0)
| order by label asc

content.query:
let es = AzMaintenance_EventServices({IncludeSynthetic})
    | where impact_start_utc between ({TimeRange:start} .. {TimeRange:end})
    | where '*' in ({Subscriptions}) or subscription_id in ({Subscriptions})
    | where '*' in ({Category}) or category in ({Category})
    | where '*' in ({Service}) or service in ({Service})
    | where '*' in ({Region}) or region in ({Region});
let iv = AzMaintenance_ResourceIntervals({IncludeSynthetic})
    | where '*' in ({Subscriptions}) or subscription_id in ({Subscriptions})
    | where '*' in ({Category}) or category in ({Category})
    | where '*' in ({Service}) or service_name in ({Service})
    | where end_utc > {TimeRange:start} and start_utc < {TimeRange:end}
    | where {IncludeUserInitiated} or not(user_initiated);
let open_u = toscalar(es | where is_open and class == "Unplanned" | summarize dcount(tracking_id));
let down_now = toscalar(iv | where state =~ "Unavailable" and is_open and not(stale_open) | summarize dcount(resource_id));
let recent = toscalar(es | where class == "Unplanned" and impact_start_utc > ago(7d) | summarize dcount(tracking_id));
let soon = toscalar(AzMaintenance_Planned({IncludeSynthetic}) | where upcoming and window_start_utc < now() + 14d | summarize dcount(tracking_id));
let stale_src = toscalar(AzMaintenance_DataHealth({IncludeSynthetic}) | where section == "ingest" and status == "STALE" | summarize count());
let att = datatable(order: int)[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
| extend status = case(order == 1, iff(open_u > 0, "bad", "good"),
                       order == 2, iff(down_now > 0, "bad", "good"),
                       order == 3, iff(recent > 0, "warn", "good"),
                       order == 4, iff(soon > 0, "info", "good"),
                       iff(stale_src > 0, "warn", "good")),
         message = case(order == 1, iff(open_u > 0, strcat(open_u, " Azure incident(s) still open"), "No Azure incidents are open right now"),
                        order == 2, iff(down_now > 0, strcat(down_now, " resource(s) unavailable right now"), "All tracked resources are available"),
                        order == 3, iff(recent > 0, strcat(recent, " unplanned event(s) in the last 7 days"), "No unplanned events in the last 7 days"),
                        order == 4, iff(soon > 0, strcat(soon, " planned maintenance notice(s) in the next 14 days"), "No planned maintenance in the next 14 days"),
                        iff(stale_src > 0, strcat(stale_src, " data source(s) have not reported in 36 hours"), "All data sources are reporting")),
         detail = case(order == 1, iff(open_u > 0, "Click to see the longest events (Timeline tab)", "Nothing to do"),
                       order == 2, iff(down_now > 0, "Click to see which resources (Resources tab)", "Nothing to do"),
                       order == 3, iff(recent > 0, "Click to see the details (Timeline tab)", "Nothing to do"),
                       order == 4, iff(soon > 0, "Click to see dates and services (Planned maintenance tab)", "Nothing to do"),
                       iff(stale_src > 0, "Numbers may be out of date. Click to open the Data health tab", "Numbers are up to date")),
         go = case(order == 1, "timeline", order == 2, "resources", order == 3, "timeline", order == 4, "planned", "health");
att
| summarize bad = countif(status == "bad"), warn = countif(status == "warn")
| project metric = case(bad > 0, "Action needed", warn > 0, "Worth a look", "All clear"),
          value = todouble(bad + warn),
          subtitle = case(bad > 0, "Something is unavailable or still open right now. See the checklist below.",
                          warn > 0, "No outright problems, but some points need a look. See the checklist below.",
                          "Nothing needs your attention right now."),
          status = case(bad > 0, "bad", warn > 0, "warn", "good"),
          go = "timeline"
content.title: Overall status
content.noDataMessage: No status information yet. See the Data health tab.

content.json:
**What this page shows**

A one-page summary for a quick review. Everything here can be opened in more detail on the other tabs.

**How to read it**

- **Unplanned events** are Azure incidents nobody scheduled. **Planned maintenance** is work Azure announced in advance.
- **Observed downtime** is the number of minutes your resources were reported *Unavailable*. It is not the same as how long an event was open (**event time open**).
- **Observed availability** is the share of time your resources were up.
- Each event is counted once, even if it affected several services or regions. The small line under a number is its weekly trend.

**What this page shows**

How things changed month by month, so you can spot busy periods and trends, plus the longest events.

**How to read it**

- The **first chart** counts events per month, orange for unplanned and blue for planned.
- The **second chart** shows the minutes your resources were actually unavailable each month.
- The **calendars** show each week as a row and each day as a square: the darker the square, the more events started that day. Orange calendar = unplanned, blue = planned.
- The two charts measure different things: a month can have many events and little or no downtime for your resources.
- The **table** lists the longest events. The bar shows how long the event was open (exposure), which is not downtime.

content.query:
let es = AzMaintenance_EventServices({IncludeSynthetic})
    | where impact_start_utc between ({TimeRange:start} .. {TimeRange:end})
    | where '*' in ({Subscriptions}) or subscription_id in ({Subscriptions})
    | where '*' in ({Category}) or category in ({Category})
    | where '*' in ({Service}) or service in ({Service})
    | where '*' in ({Region}) or region in ({Region});
let days = es
    | where class == "Unplanned"
    | summarize n = dcount(tracking_id) by day = startofday(impact_start_utc)
    | extend week = startofweek(day), dow = toint(dayofweek(day) / 1d)
    | summarize Sun = sumif(n, dow == 0), Mon = sumif(n, dow == 1), Tue = sumif(n, dow == 2), Wed = sumif(n, dow == 3),
                Thu = sumif(n, dow == 4), Fri = sumif(n, dow == 5), Sat = sumif(n, dow == 6) by week;
range week from startofweek({TimeRange:start}) to startofweek({TimeRange:end}) step 7d
| join kind=leftouter days on week
| project week, Sun = coalesce(Sun, long(0)), Mon = coalesce(Mon, long(0)), Tue = coalesce(Tue, long(0)), Wed = coalesce(Wed, long(0)),
          Thu = coalesce(Thu, long(0)), Fri = coalesce(Fri, long(0)), Sat = coalesce(Sat, long(0))
| order by week desc

content.json:
**What this page shows**

Each Azure service you use, grouped by type, with how often it had problems and how available it was.

**How to read it**

- **IaaS** = infrastructure you manage (virtual machines, disks). **PaaS** = managed services (App Service, containers). The other groups are Network, Data, Identity and AI.
- **Events** = number of incidents and maintenance notices. **Typical / long event** = how long events lasted: half were shorter than *typical*, 9 in 10 were shorter than *long*.
- **Downtime** = minutes your resources of that service were unavailable. **Availability** is coloured green (99.9% or better), yellow (99% or better) or red.
- **SLA not set** means no SLA percentage has been entered for that service yet. SLA values are never guessed; they come from `reference/service_catalog.csv` with a source.
- The **hexagon map** shows each service as a cell, grouped by type: the redder the cell, the more events it had. In the scorecard, the small line is the weekly trend. **Click a row** to see that service's events underneath.

content.title: ⏱️ Services with the most unavailable minutes
content.noDataMessage: 🎉 No downtime recorded for these services in the selected range.

content.query:
let es = AzMaintenance_EventServices({IncludeSynthetic})
    | where impact_start_utc between ({TimeRange:start} .. {TimeRange:end})
    | where '*' in ({Subscriptions}) or subscription_id in ({Subscriptions})
    | where '*' in ({Category}) or category in ({Category})
    | where '*' in ({Service}) or service in ({Service})
    | where '*' in ({Region}) or region in ({Region});
let per = es
    | where class in ("Planned", "Unplanned")
    | summarize events = dcount(tracking_id) by service, category;
let mx = toscalar(per | summarize max(events));
per
| project Name = service, Events = events, Intensity = iff(mx > 0, round(events * 100.0 / mx, 1), 0.0), Group = category
| order by Events desc
| take 60

content.json:
**What this page shows**

Which Azure regions were affected by events in the selected range.

**How to read it**

- Darker or larger bubbles on the map mean more events in that region.
- One event can affect several regions, so the same event appears on several rows. **Do not add the rows up to get a total**; use the Overview page for totals.
- Use this to see whether problems cluster in the regions you rely on.
- **Click a row in the table** to list the events of that region underneath it.

content.json:
**What this page shows**

A closer look at individual resources: which ones were unavailable and when.

**How to read it**

- The **chart** lists the resources with the most unavailable minutes.
- The **table** lists every period a resource was *Unavailable* or *Degraded*, with start, end, length, whether it was planned or unplanned, and whether it is still ongoing.
- Periods you caused yourself (for example stopping a VM) are hidden unless you switch on *Include user-initiated downtime* at the top.
- A period that has stayed open for more than 3 days with no recovery signal is marked **Stale** and is not counted (this is usually a resource that was deleted or scaled in).

content.query:
let iv = AzMaintenance_ResourceIntervals({IncludeSynthetic})
    | where '*' in ({Subscriptions}) or subscription_id in ({Subscriptions})
    | where '*' in ({Category}) or category in ({Category})
    | where '*' in ({Service}) or service_name in ({Service})
    | where end_utc > {TimeRange:start} and start_utc < {TimeRange:end}
    | where {IncludeUserInitiated} or not(user_initiated);
iv
| where state =~ "Unavailable" and not(stale_open)
| summarize intervals = count(), downtime_min = round(sum(minutes), 1) by resource_id, service_name
| top 10 by downtime_min desc
| project resource = tostring(split(resource_id, "/")[-1]), service_name, intervals, downtime_min
content.title: 🔥 Resources with the most unavailable minutes
content.noDataMessage: 🎉 No Resource Health downtime recorded in the selected range.

content.query:
let iv = AzMaintenance_ResourceIntervals({IncludeSynthetic})
    | where '*' in ({Subscriptions}) or subscription_id in ({Subscriptions})
    | where '*' in ({Category}) or category in ({Category})
    | where '*' in ({Service}) or service_name in ({Service})
    | where end_utc > {TimeRange:start} and start_utc < {TimeRange:end}
    | where {IncludeUserInitiated} or not(user_initiated);
iv
| extend status = case(stale_open, "Stale (not counted)", is_open, "Ongoing", "Recovered"),
         resource = tostring(split(resource_id, "/")[-1])
| project status, resource, service_name, state, class, start_utc, end_utc = iff(is_open, datetime(null), end_utc), minutes, cause, classification_basis
| order by start_utc desc
| take 500

content.json:
**What this page shows**

Maintenance that Azure announced in advance, what is coming up, and what has already happened.

**How to read it**

- **Upcoming** lists maintenance that has not started yet. The *days until* colour shows urgency: red within 3 days, orange within 7 days, blue later.
- **History** lists maintenance in the selected time range. **Scheduled hours** is the planned window. It is *not* downtime; most of the time nothing is noticed.
- **Notice (days)** is how far ahead the notice was first seen by this ledger. It can be shorter than the real notice if collection started late, and is blank if the ledger first saw the notice after the work had started.
- **Realised downtime** is the minutes your resources were actually unavailable during the window, or *not measured* when there is no data.
- The last table lists planned VM maintenance and whether a reboot was mentioned.

content.title: 📊 Maintenance at a glance
content.noDataMessage: No planned maintenance in the ledger yet.

content.query:
AzMaintenance_Planned({IncludeSynthetic})
| where '*' in ({Subscriptions}) or subscription_id in ({Subscriptions})
| summarize arg_min(window_start_utc, *) by tracking_id
| where window_start_utc between ({TimeRange:start} .. ({TimeRange:end} + 120d))
| summarize notices = dcount(tracking_id) by month = startofmonth(window_start_utc)
| order by month asc
content.title: 📅 Maintenance notices per month
content.noDataMessage: No planned maintenance in the selected range.

content.query:
AzMaintenance_Planned({IncludeSynthetic})
| where upcoming and ('*' in ({Subscriptions}) or subscription_id in ({Subscriptions}))
| summarize arg_min(window_start_utc, *) by tracking_id
| project days_until = round(todouble(datetime_diff("hour", window_start_utc, now())) / 24.0, 1), event_title,
          services = strcat_array(services, ", "), regions = strcat_array(regions, ", "), window_start_utc, window_end_utc, scheduled_h
| order by window_start_utc asc
content.title: ⏭️ Upcoming maintenance
content.noDataMessage: ✅ No upcoming planned maintenance.

content.query:
AzMaintenance_Planned({IncludeSynthetic})
| where not(upcoming) and window_start_utc between ({TimeRange:start} .. {TimeRange:end})
| where '*' in ({Subscriptions}) or subscription_id in ({Subscriptions})
| summarize arg_min(window_start_utc, *) by tracking_id
| project event_title, services = strcat_array(services, ", "), window_start_utc, scheduled_h, lead_time_days, realised_downtime_min, affected_resources
| order by window_start_utc desc
content.title: ⏮️ Maintenance history
content.noDataMessage: No planned maintenance in the selected range.

content.query:
AzVmAnnotations_CL
| where {IncludeSynthetic} or is_synthetic != true
| where category =~ "Planned" and occurred_utc between ({TimeRange:start} .. {TimeRange:end})
| where '*' in ({Subscriptions}) or subscription_id in ({Subscriptions})
| summarize arg_max(ingested_utc, *) by row_key
| project resource_id, region, annotation_name, reason, context, occurred_utc, reboot_mentioned = (reason has "reboot" or annotation_name has "reboot")
| order by occurred_utc desc
content.title: 💻 VM planned maintenance notes
content.noDataMessage: No VM annotations. The VM annotation module is optional and needs VMs in scope.

content.json:
**What this page shows**

After a major incident Azure publishes a public report called a Post Incident Review (PIR). This page lists them as a benchmark for context.

**How to read it**

- This is **Azure-wide, not your estate**. It shows what happened across Azure, whether or not your resources were affected.
- Only large, broad incidents get a public PIR, so small issues are not here.
- **Incident window** is how long the incident lasted, read from the report text. If a window could not be read, the table says so in *Window read*.

content.title: 📊 Azure-wide at a glance
content.noDataMessage: No public PIRs loaded.

content.query:
AzMaintenance_PirBaseline({IncludeSynthetic})
| summarize pirs = count() by year = tostring(year), category
| order by year asc
content.title: 📅 Public PIRs per year
content.noDataMessage: No public PIRs loaded.

content.query:
AzMaintenance_PirBaseline({IncludeSynthetic})
| summarize pirs = count(), with_window = countif(isnotnull(duration_h)), median_h = round(percentile(duration_h, 50), 1),
            p90_h = round(percentile(duration_h, 90), 1), max_h = round(max(duration_h), 1) by category
| order by pirs desc
content.title: ⏱️ Incident length by category (hours)
content.noDataMessage: No public PIRs loaded.

content.query:
AzMaintenance_PirBaseline({IncludeSynthetic})
| project published_date, category, event_title, duration_h, parse_status, tracking_id
| order by published_date desc

content.json:
**What this page shows**

A guide to how much downtime to plan for, based on what has actually happened in your own history. It is evidence, not a forecast or a promise.

**How to read it**

- Pick a **service** and **region**. The tiles show a *typical year* (P50) and a *bad year* (P90) in hours of downtime.
- The icon on the tile is the **confidence**: green = high, blue = medium, amber = low or insufficient history. Few past events means low confidence.
- The charts compare categories: your estate on the left, the **Azure-wide PIR baseline** on the right (not about your estate, shown for context when your own history is thin).
- **SLA allowance** is how much downtime the SLA permits per year, shown only when an SLA has been entered.
- **Composite SLA**: type the SLAs of the parts of your solution. *Serial* means every part must be up (availability goes down). *Redundant* means any one part is enough (availability goes up).

parameters.name: PlannerService
parameters.label: Service
parameters.query:
let rows = union
    (AzMaintenance_EventServices({IncludeSynthetic}) | summarize by service),
    (AzMaintenance_Catalog({IncludeSynthetic}) | summarize by service = service_name)
    | summarize by service
    | project value = service, label = service;
let n = toscalar(rows | count);
rows
| union (print value = "(no data yet)", label = "(no data yet)" | where n == 0)
| order by label asc

parameters.name: PlannerRegion
parameters.label: Region

parameters.name: CompositeMode
parameters.label: Composition
parameters.jsonData: [{"value": "serial", "label": "Serial (all must be up)", "selected": true}, {"value": "redundant", "label": "Redundant (any one is enough)", "selected": false}]

**What this page shows**

A check that the ledger itself is working and how far back its data goes. Look here first if the numbers on other pages look wrong or empty.

**How to read it**

- **ingest** rows show when each data source last updated. A red cross (STALE) means no successful update in the last 36 hours.
- **coverage** rows show the earliest data held for each source, so you know how much history the numbers are based on.
- **quality** shows problems reading data, for example public reports whose incident window could not be read.
- **subscriptions** compares the subscriptions that have data with the subscriptions configured.

content.json:
### About this workbook
**Azure Maintenance Ledger** gives a customer one place to see the planned and unplanned maintenance of their Azure IaaS and PaaS services, and the downtime to expect, from a durable history. Azure itself only keeps Service Health and Resource Health data for a limited time (90 days to 1 year); the ledger keeps it for 730 days so trends can be reviewed after Azure has aged the data out.

**Purpose**
- Keep a durable record of Service Health events, Resource Health downtime and public Azure post-incident reviews (PIRs).
- Separate **planned** from **unplanned** events, **IaaS** from **PaaS** services, and **exposure** (the event window) from **downtime** (minutes a resource was Unavailable).
- Report observed availability against the SLA (where an SLA has been supplied) and an evidence-based expected-downtime planning range, always with sample size, window and confidence.

Figures are evidence from history. They are not a forecast, a guarantee or a billing-grade availability measure.

### Colours and icons
- 🟧 **Orange** = unplanned. 🟦 **Blue** = planned.
- ✅ **Green tick** = fine. ⚠️ **Amber warning** = take a look. ❌ **Red** = act. ℹ️ **Blue info** = for your information.
- Bars inside tables show relative size within that column. Colour-filled cells show how good or bad the value is.

### Method
1. **Intervals.** Resource Health: per resourceId, order events by time; open an interval when currentHealthStatus becomes Unavailable (type Downtime) from a non-Unavailable state; close it on Available. Ignore duplicate Active/Updated rows and Unknown states. Open intervals end at now() and are flagged open. Merge overlapping intervals per resource before summing. Exclude cause = UserInitiated.
2. **Classification.** Service Health: ServiceIssue/Incident -> unplanned; PlannedMaintenance/Maintenance -> planned. Resource Health interval: VM annotation category if present; else planned if it overlaps a PlannedMaintenance window for the same subscription, service and region; else unplanned. Always store classification_basis (vm_annotation | overlaps_planned_event | default).
3. **Event counting.** One event per TrackingId in totals (dcount). Expand services and regions only for per-service and per-region views, and never sum those rows into a total.
4. **Observed availability** = 1 - sum(merged downtime minutes) / (resource_count x window minutes), with resource_count from the latest AzInventoryCounts_CL. Mark as approximate when resources were created or deleted in the window.
5. **SLA allowance** = (1 - sla) x window minutes, only where sla_percent is set; otherwise show "SLA not set".
6. **Planning range** (analytics/forecast.py, run daily). Scope fallback: service+region, then service, then category. Window W = trailing 365 days (minimum 90). n = distinct unplanned events; lambda = n / (W/365). Durations = Resource Health impact minutes per event where available, else Service Health exposure minutes; label which. Simulate 10,000 years: N ~ Poisson(lambda), sum N durations drawn with replacement; report mean, P50 and P90 annual hours. Confidence (heuristic, configurable in config/forecast.yaml): insufficient if n < 3 or W < 90 d; low if n is 3-5 or W < 365 d; medium if n is 6-11; high if n >= 12 and W >= 365 d. For insufficient and low, also show the public-PIR baseline, labelled "Azure-wide, not your estate". Never print a single number without n, window and confidence.
7. **Planned maintenance:** report notices per year, scheduled window, notice lead time (publication to window start), and realised downtime from Resource Health overlap (or "not measured").
8. **Composite SLA:** serial = product of availabilities; redundant = 1 - product of (1 - availability). Python (analytics/sla.py) and KQL must both pass the SLA test vectors in AGENTS.md A2.
9. **PIR windows:** parse the first "Between/From <time> ... <date>" sentence: two HH:MM UTC times and one or two dates ("30 September 2026" and "September 30, 2026"); if there is one date and end < start, roll the end to the next day; reject windows longer than 14 days; set parse_status ok or unparsed; reference/pir_overrides.csv can supply a window (parse_status manual).

### Caveats
- Azure keeps Service Health 90 days to 1 year and Resource Health 30 days; the ledger starts when collection starts (see Data health coverage).
- Resource Health records transitions to or from Unhealthy and states lasting more than 15 minutes; Unknown states and very short blips are not recorded.
- Planned/unplanned classification of a Resource Health interval uses the VM annotation, else overlap with a planned event for the same subscription and service (region is not available on Resource Health rows).
- Observed availability depends on the resource counts of the latest inventory snapshot and is marked approximate when counts changed.
- Public PIRs are fetched from an undocumented endpoint and cover broad-impact incidents only.
- Planning ranges are evidence from history, not a forecast or an SLA.
